summary: Dedicated pool stripe saturation causing affinity oscillation and increased fallback latency
description: Issue summary: NoteCorp is observing elevated tail latency and fallback routing to lower-tier model variants starting 2026-03-12 08:45 UTC. Impact: customer P1 - sustained p99 generation latency increased from ~270ms to 2.1s and throughput dropped ~45% for pinned dedicated routes during peak window. Environment: prod us-east dedicated pool (reserve id: dp-11-eus). Observed behavior: autoplace scheduler shows stripe-level saturation where a subset of GPU stripes report high attach and prefetch times and oscillate between 'available' and 'degraded' over 10-30s windows, triggering autoscaler shrink/grow cycles and causing the platform to route traffic to fallback variants. Expected behavior: balanced stripe assignment, stable autoscaler decisions, and sub-400ms p99 for pinned routes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NoteCorp's pinned route to redwood/llama-2-13b on the dedicated pool dp-11-eus during the weekday peak (08:30-09:30 UTC). 2) Replay production-ish burst profile: 200 concurrent short streams (avg tokens/request 40) with 300ms inter-arrival jitter for 20 minutes. 3) Observe scheduler / allocator metrics and the autoscaler decision logs. 4) Compare p99 latency before/after the 08:45 window.
observed_metrics_and_logs:
- allocator/stripe/attach_time p95: 480ms -> p99: 2.2s during incident window.
- autoscaler/actions: shrink at 08:47, grow at 08:49 repeated 6x over 20m.
- serving-runtime logs show repeated kv-prefetch timeouts and worker worker-threads in 'stalled' state intermittently.
- perf dashboard: GPU utilization skewed: 3 stripes at 95%+ while 5 stripes idle ~5-15%.
- connection trace: multiple short-streams hold ephemeral connections open for 1.2s longer than normal, increasing slot fragmentation.
- relevant logs: /var/log/serve/worker-attach.log (snippets linked in confluence page).
hypotheses_and_investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: noisy tenant in the same reserved pool is creating ephemeral microbursts that over-index a subset of stripes due to affinity heuristics. Hypothesis 2: scheduler's stripe balancing heuristic over-corrects during short-window bursts, creating oscillation and autoscaler thrash. Hypothesis 3: a newly-deployed sidecar (metrics-collector v2.1) is intermittently causing IO spikes on certain hosts resulting in stripe-level I/O backpressure. Investigations performed: checked host-level iostat and found elevated nvme write IO on 4 hosts during the window; cross-referenced with deployment history and saw metrics-collector v2.1 rolled out to those hosts 2026-03-11. Snapshot of autoscaler decision logs attached to ticket. Temporary isolation test: we removed NoteCorp traffic and replayed only suspected noisy tenant traffic — stripe imbalance reproduced.

2026-03-12 13:10 - Runtime Eng (Priya Singh): Added temporary affinity smoothing parameter to dp-11-eus to damp oscillation; saw p99 drop from 2.1s to 640ms in canary window.

2026-03-13 09:50 - Autoscaler Eng (Omar Li): Investigating shrink/grow hysteresis thresholds; noted we need better cooldown logic to avoid responding to sub-30s variance. PR drafted: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/274.
2026-03-14 01:30 - SRE: Completed a host-level remediation (reverted metrics-collector v2.1 to v2.0 on affected hosts). Observed reduction in nvme IO spikes and more even stripe utilization.
temporary_mitigation_and_workaround:
- Enabled affinity smoothing on dp-11-eus to reduce aggressive rebalancing (rolling change).
- Throttled noisy tenant identified by tenant id tn-449 for 1 hour during peak windows to reduce ephemeral microbursts.
- Reverted metrics-collector to v2.0 on 4 affected hosts and scheduled a controlled rollout with IO limits.
- Adjusted autoscaler cooldown from 30s to 120s in the dedicated pool staging for testing.
resolution_notes: Partial resolution: reverting metrics-collector and enabling affinity smoothing restored stable stripe distribution and reduced p99 from 2.1s to ~380ms under replayed load. Autoscaler hysteresis change prevented thrash in staging; PR merged to prod (see related PR). Next steps: 1) full rollout of autoscaler cooldown change after additional soak; 2) implement tenant-level noisy detection and automated soft-throttle; 3) postmortem runbook to include checklist for sidecar IO regressions. Will keep ticket open until full rollout and customer sign-off.
